name: VHS
notes: 2026-11-01: Renders .tape scripts of terminal sessions to GIF, MP4, WebM or frames via ttyd and Chromium.
2026-11-01: Records in real time, so output is NOT a pure function of t; treat as a source asset.
2026-11-24: Toolkit guide written from partial evidence (MP4, text golden); PNG frames are cropped and frame counts vary, so gate on the text golden.

evidence.result: Headless tape (640x360, FontSize 20, Framerate 10, TypingSpeed 100ms): MP4 h264 640x360, 3.84 s and 4.04 s over two runs; golden text identical across runs, with both commands and outputs; final frame shows typed text (33,696 changed pixels vs first). Failed predeclared checks: PNG frames 494x208 not 640x360; PNG frames 78 and 82 (cursor and text families); MP4 frames 96 and 101 vs 39 +/- 10. Chrome 158.0.8127.37 via vhs, ttyd 1.7.7.
evidence.scope: Headless tape to MP4, PNG frames and text golden; typed text in golden and final frame; PNG 494x208 and frame counts outside predeclared checks; macOS arm64, real-time, no seek.

summary: Go CLI that executes .tape scripts in a virtual terminal and records terminal output to GIF, MP4, WebM or still/text outputs. Tapes set dimensions, font and framerate and issue keystrokes, commands and waits. Its strength is repeatable scripted terminal demonstrations and golden-file capture; it records a real-time session rather than a frame-seekable animation.
use_when: Capture a CLI walkthrough from a scripted terminal session
Use over manual screen recording when the terminal sequence can be scripted
avoid_when: Use VCR browser capture for deterministic browser scenes
Use direct terminal rendering for static terminal artwork without timed interaction

assessment.rationale: VHS v0.12.1 released 2026-09-24; repository documents current CI and installation. Requires ttyd and FFmpeg; MIT. Scripted terminal demos fill a distinct capture job, though real-time execution is not seek-safe.
